fields.v: Jarmak, S. (2026). Engineering Reliable Coding Agents: Evaluating and Operating the System Around the Model. Version 1.0.0, August 2026. arXiv:2608.13867v1 [cs.SE], 14 Aug 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2608.13867v1 [cs.SE]; self-published technical review and engineering monograph (313 pages, web edition and companion repository), no published venue

Not stated on the title page. The data statement says the author built and operates CodeScaleBench 'at the vendor whose retrieval product supplies one of its two arms' (repository github.com/sourcegraph/CodeScaleBench, i.e. Sourcegraph, industry)

Review; secondary: Conceptual — structured multivocal review (164 scholarly works, 100 practitioner records, 29 benchmark records, 17 author-system case records) synthesized into a reliability dependency chain framework and a catalog of 206 reliability records (193 gated practices, 56 developed in depth, 13 research leads), with runnable evaluation protocols and author-system measurements as illustrations

No SDD approach evaluated. Engineering practices for coding-agent systems (ERCA-NNN catalog, v1.0.0), including 'consolidated-spec restarts' (restart a drifting run from one authoritative consolidated specification plus an execution handoff) and a no-file baseline for standing repository context files (AGENTS.md-type), citing Gloaguen et al. (2026) and Khatri (2026) null results

For the consolidated-spec restart practice: a consolidated specification (settled requirements, constraints, definitions, interfaces, open questions; versioned, superseding earlier proposals), an execution handoff (repository state, completed changes, current failures, verification done, raw artifacts) and a starting instruction naming the authoritative sources. Elsewhere: evaluation records (paired per-item outcomes, cost, model/harness/prompt versions), failure taxonomy, decision rules fixed before results

Not an SDD flow. Dependency chain of six layers: measurement, grading, containment and recovery, retrieval and context, review and accountability, allocation and cost. 'Minimum pass': rerun a decision with paired baseline (3 runs per item), record success/cost/configuration, exercise permitted and prohibited actions, verify a completion claim, read 20 failed runs, fix a decision rule before the next promotion

Treated as an engineered control (Part V): verification interfaces, risk-based escalation, autonomy widened one action class at a time, effective gates that can change execution, accountable ownership; for spec restarts, the restart boundary belongs to the control plane, not to the failing run
N/A (review; not run as an SDD approach). Author-system measurements on own systems (CodeScaleBench retrieval arms, 199-trace diagnostic corpus, 1,286-item fleet ledger) as illustrations
Not classifiable (system reliability review; the author uses 'consolidated specification' for restarts but no SDD levels)
Both / not restricted; operating conditions assumed: large organizational codebases with many repositories (author measurements on repositories of millions to tens of millions of lines)

Review corpus: 164 scholarly works (118 base, 11 update audit, 9 SE coverage probe, 21 distributed-systems synthesis, plus targeted additions), 100 practitioner records, 29 benchmark records, 17 author-system cases; 244 candidate practices -> 214 retained -> 206 records. Author measurement: CodeScaleBench 370 paired tasks in 20 suites, 46 anchor repositories (56 distinct), nine languages, repositories up to ~35M lines (Chromium)
General software engineering in large organizations (enterprise-scale, multi-repository work)
N/A (no participants). Intended reader: senior engineers, evaluation leads, technical owners

Recommended (not measured as results): inference and tool cost, tokens, model calls, elapsed time, cost per completed/accepted task, labeling and adjudication hours, reviewer queue time; cost-accuracy frontier for configuration selection

Recommended: execution-based acceptance checks, paired per-item outcomes, pass@k and pass^k (k=3 to start), verified resolution separate from submission; in the author measurement, paired end-to-end reward on CodeScaleBench
None specific (design review discussed qualitatively)
Recommended: reviewer queue time, labeling and adjudication hours, approval and modification rates for autonomy calibration

Retrieval metrics (Precision@10, Recall@k, share of tasks with at least one needed file), effective context length, grader agreement (Cohen's/Fleiss's kappa), recovery under fault injection, failure taxonomy labels

Review: retrieval via SciX/SciX Agent, Code Intelligence Digest (author-operated), OpenAlex probe, DBLP title census; LLM-assisted claim extraction, evidence-group proposal and challenge passes, final decisions by the author alone; no inter-rater agreement (blinded packet released for external graders). Author measurements: automatic benchmark scoring with bootstrap CIs; trace corpus analysed by the author

N/A for the review as a whole (no configuration run as a study). Author-system illustration (Ch. 12, CodeScaleBench, 370 paired tasks): (1) baseline arm, local repositories with built-in file tools, agent and model not stated in the text: Precision@10 0.095, Recall@10 0.120, tasks with at least one needed file 0.33; (2) retrieval arm, same code through a retrieval server (author's employer's product), agent and model not stated: Precision@10 0.313, Recall@10 0.272, share 0.56; paired end-to-end reward difference +0.0349 (bootstrap 95% CI +0.0130 to +0.0579, author says the CI understates uncertainty). No success criterion stated by the authors; quality and cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors

N/A (review). Recommends paired comparisons on identical task versions, cheapest credible baseline, k=3 runs per item for screening, power analysis sized to the smallest decision-relevant effect, pinned model/harness/prompt/decoding versions, decision rules fixed before execution, no-file baseline for context files

Synthesis: many apparent model failures originate in the surrounding system; improvements at one layer often do not propagate to end-to-end outcomes (e.g. retrieval metrics roughly doubled while end-to-end reward moved +0.035); advertised context is not usable context; standing context files showed no task benefit and ~20% added cost in Gloaguen et al. (2026), with Khatri (2026) bounding any correctness effect to about 10-15 points; Spearman -0.004 between urgency rank and having strong evidence across 52 ranked practices
N/A

Search structured, not exhaustive; ACM DL, IEEE Xplore and Scopus searches not performed (access failures); original interactive queries not fully logged (reconstructed); single-author adjudication, no inter-rater agreement; evidence uneven, recent capability measurements age quickly; practitioner reports prone to selection and survivorship bias; Part VI is a research agenda by transfer from adjacent fields; author-system cases are illustrations, not independent evidence. Gaps: controlled comparison of isolation and authority designs against observed incidents; a recovery benchmark with published fault menu

Companion repository https://github.com/sjarmak/engineering-reliable-coding-agents (catalog, evidence ledger, thread protocols, screening decisions, checksums, blinded grading packet); CodeScaleBench public (github.com/sourcegraph/CodeScaleBench, tag v1-mixed371); 199-trace corpus and 1,286-item fleet ledger not redistributed. Conflict of interest: the retrieval measurement compares the author's employer's retrieval product with a baseline (author acknowledges, treats as illustration). Single author. Cut-off 26 Jul 2026, update audit to 6 Aug 2026. Page references give printed page and file page; only front matter, Ch. 4, 12, 14, 20 and data statement read in full for this draft (313-page document). No pre-registration. Partly (0.5): entry criterion (at least one measured result, mechanism, incident, benchmark property or practice relevant to coding-agent reliability) and screening exclusions stated, but broad; distributed-systems and later additions entered by targeted citation-driven selection outside the thread protocol

rev.why: The entry criterion and screening exclusions are explicitly stated (p. xvii), which under Kitchenham's DARE reading could be Yes; Partly rests on the targeted citation-driven admissions (distributed-systems synthesis, post-cutoff case) that bypassed the thread protocol.

fields.warn: Os critérios de inclusão estão explícitos (p. xvii), mas cerca de 30 fontes entraram por seleção dirigida fora do protocolo. Decide se isto baixa DARE1 para Partly ou se fica Yes.

fields.v: Partly (0.5): several sources (SciX/arXiv, practitioner digest, OpenAlex probe of eight SE venues, DBLP census) and cut-off dates given; ACM DL, IEEE Xplore and Scopus not searched; exact queries not preserved; author states search is not exhaustive
Partly (0.5): evidence graded into strong, directional, corroborating and null/conflicting per scoped claim with challenge passes and a downgrade audit; single author, no inter-rater agreement

rev.why: Evidence is graded per scoped claim (strong/directional/corroborating/null) with explicit definitions, challenge passes and a downgrade audit (p. xvii-xviii); this is a defined quality assessment, but per claim rather than per primary study and by a single adjudicator, so Yes or Partly are both defensible.

fields.warn: A qualidade é avaliada por afirmação (quatro grupos de evidência definidos), não por estudo primário, e só pelo autor. Confirma nas p. xvii-xviii se aceitas isto como Yes ou mantens Partly.
